heroHeadline: OPERATIONAL WEEK CONTINUES: DENMARK DEPLOYS CONSCRIPTS TO GREENLAND UNDER NATO'S 'ARCTIC SENTRY' (SEP 2), HMS QUEEN ELIZABETH SAILS AS NATO COMMAND SHIP (SEP 5); PENTAGON POSTURE REVIEW STILL AWAITS SEP 18 COLBY BRIEFING, NO NEW ARTICLE 5 DEVELOPMENTS SINCE AUG 31
heroSubtitle: As of September 6, 2026, the Article 5 credibility question that has dominated the NATO-US tracker all year saw no new public developments this week beyond the August 31 Bild/Telegraph reporting and Baltic/Nordic pushback already on record. Instead, the week's verified developments were operational: Denmark deployed conscripts to Greenland for the first time in recent history on September 2 as part of Arctic Endurance, a roughly 400-troop, 10-nation exercise under NATO's Arctic Sentry mission launched this year to ease alliance tensions stemming from Trump's repeated demands that the US acquire Greenland — demands Denmark and Greenland continue to reject. Separately, the Royal Navy carrier HMS Queen Elizabeth sailed from Portsmouth on September 5 for a three-month deployment as NATO's Allied Response Force command ship, underscoring continued European capability investment even as US force levels remain unresolved. The EU's SAFE defense-loan instrument also reached a concrete milestone in late August, with Romania (€2.5B), Bulgaria (€489M) and Latvia (€525M) receiving their first pre-financing disbursements — over €3.5B combined. NATO Secretary General Rutte, at a September 2 press conference with European Commission President von der Leyen, called Russia 'increasingly reckless,' citing eastern-flank drone and missile incursions and an alleged hybrid attack on a German defense factory in Leipzig. NATO allies' August 29 deadline to respond to the Pentagon's access-and-loyalty questionnaire has passed without a consolidated public accounting, and Reuters continues to report four troop-level options are due to Hegseth by November 6, with the top US general in Europe due to brief Under Secretary Colby on force-level options by September 18.
